payload.text:
Design and develop a premium luxury e-commerce website along with a full admin dashboard for a clock brand named “AEVO”.

Brand & Visual Style:
- Brand Name: AEVO
- Theme: Luxury, minimal, modern
- Color Palette: Soft pastel colors (cream, beige, blush, light grey, muted gold accents)
- Typography: Elegant serif for headings, clean sans-serif for body text
- Overall Feel: High-end, smooth, calm, premium, Apple-like polish
- Animations: Subtle micro-interactions, smooth page transitions, soft hover effects
- UI/Explainability: Clean, spacious layouts with strong visual hierarchy
- UX Priority: Very smooth, fast, intuitive, mobile-first design

Homepage (Landing Page):
- Full-width hero section with auto-changing image banners (carousel)
  - Banner slides highlight: Latest Models, Best Selling, Limited Edition, Offers, New Arrivals
  - Smooth fade / slide transitions with elegant text overlay
- Clear CTA buttons: “Shop Now”, “Explore Collection”, “View Offers”
- Sections on homepage:
  - Latest Models
  - Best Selling Clocks
  - Featured / Limited Edition
  - Offers & Discounts
  - Category Highlights (Men, Women, Wall Clocks, Smart Clocks, Luxury Series)
- Luxury storytelling section explaining AEVO brand philosophy
- Customer reviews & ratings (minimal luxury cards)
- Newsletter subscription
- Footer with brand info, policies, contact, social links

Product Listing Pages:
- Category-wise product listing
- Filters:
  - Price range
  - Category
  - Strap type
  - Dial size
  - Color
  - Availability
  - New / Best Seller / Discount
- Sorting options:
  - Latest
  - Price: Low to High
  - Price: High to Low
  - Best Selling
- Product cards with:
  - High-quality images
  - Hover image swap
  - Quick add to cart
  - Wishlist icon

Product Detail Page:
- Large high-resolution product gallery
- Zoom & image slider
- Product details:
  - Model name
  - Price (original + discounted if applicable)
  - Specifications
  - Material
  - Warranty information
- Stock availability
- Ratings & reviews
- Add to cart & buy now buttons
- Related products section

Cart & Checkout:
- Smooth cart page with quantity control
- Promo / coupon code support
- Secure checkout
- Multiple payment options
- Order summary
- Confirmation page with order tracking info

User Features:
- User authentication (login / signup)
- Wishlist
- Order history
- Profile management
- Address management
- Order tracking

Admin Panel (Dashboard):
- Secure admin login
- Dashboard overview:
  - Total sales
  - Orders
  - Revenue
  - Users
- Product management:
  - Add / edit / delete products
  - Upload multiple images
  - Set categories
  - Mark products as Latest / Best Selling / Offer / Featured
- Order management:
  - View orders
  - Update order status
  - Track deliveries
- Offer & discount management
- Banner management:
  - Upload and control homepage image sliders
- User management
- Inventory & stock control
- Analytics & sales reports
- Coupon management

Technical & Performance Requirements:
- Fully responsive (mobile, tablet, desktop)
- Fast loading & optimized images
- SEO-friendly structure
- Smooth animations without performance drop
- Clean, scalable codebase
- Modern tech stack support (React / Next.js preferred)

Goal:
Create a visually stunning, luxury clock e-commerce experience that feels premium, smooth, trustworthy, and conversion-focused while remaining simple and elegant for users and powerful for admins.

**Defining AEVO's Brand Identity**

I'm now zeroing in on AEVO's brand. I'm visualizing a luxury aesthetic through minimal, modern clocks. The color palette I'm envisioning leans toward pastels: cream, beige, blush, light grey, and a touch of muted gold. I've begun to conceptualize the website structure. Homepage designs include a hero carousel, featured sections, storytelling elements, and a newsletter sign-up. I'm planning out the Product Listing Page with filters and sorting options and the Product Detail Page to showcase a gallery, product details, and recommendations.


**Developing AEVO's Tech Stack**

I'm now deep-diving into the technical architecture. I'm focusing on React 18+ with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS for the frontend. Lucide icons will probably be used, along with Recharts for the admin dashboard. The project structure is beginning to form with key files like `index.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `types.ts`, and so on. Data models for Product, Order, User, and Banner are in the works. State management will likely use React Context, for demo purposes.


**Refining Navigation & Mock Data**

I'm presently focusing on navigation with HashRouter and implementing robust mock data for realistic admin panel visuals. I'm incorporating an "Admin Mode" toggle or separate routes for clarity. I'm also adding auto-play functionality to the hero carousel and planning hover effects for the product grid. Recharts will be implemented to visualize sales data in the admin dashboard. I'm keeping the need for metadata to a minimum.

payload.text:
Design and develop a minimal, luxury e-commerce website with an admin panel for a premium clock brand named “AEVO”.

Design Philosophy:
- Style: Ultra-minimal, luxury, modern
- Layout: Hero section + full product cards grid ONLY
- No storytelling, no about section, no blog, no extra layouts
- Focus entirely on product cards and buying flow
- Color theme: Soft pastel luxury palette (cream, off-white, muted beige, light grey, subtle gold accents)
- UI feel: Premium, smooth, calm, high-end
- UX: Extremely simple, fast, and intuitive
- Animations: Very subtle, smooth, luxury micro-interactions only

Hero Section (Top Only):
- Full-width hero with auto-changing image banners (carousel)
- Banner transitions: smooth fade / slide
- Each banner highlights:
  - Latest Models
  - Best Selling
  - Limited Offers
  - New Arrivals
- Minimal text overlay
- Single CTA button: “Shop Clocks”

Main Content (Immediately After Hero):
- Full-width luxury product grid (NO other sections)
- All products displayed as premium cards
- Card-based layout only

Product Card Design:
- Soft rounded corners
- Glass / soft shadow card effect
- Pastel background cards
- Smooth hover animation:
  - Slight lift
  - Shadow enhancement
  - Image zoom
- Card contains:
  - High-quality clock image
  - Model name
  - Price (and discount if applicable)
  - Small tag (Latest / Best Seller / Offer)
  - “Buy Now” button (primary)
  - Wishlist icon (minimal)

Product Grid Features:
- Toggle / tabs above grid:
  - All
  - Latest
  - Best Selling
  - Offers
- Minimal filter (optional):
  - Price
  - Category
- Smooth loading animation for cards
- Infinite scroll or smooth pagination

Buy Flow:
- Clicking “Buy Now” opens:
  - Quick product detail modal OR product page
- Simple product view:
  - Image gallery
  - Price
  - Quantity selector
  - Buy Now / Add to Cart
- Clean, distraction-free checkout
- Fast order confirmation

Admin Panel (Minimal & Powerful):
- Secure admin login
- Dashboard with:
  - Total orders
  - Sales
  - Revenue
- Product management:
  - Add / edit / delete products
  - Upload product images
  - Set price & discount
  - Mark as Latest / Best Seller / Offer
- Homepage control:
  - Manage hero banner images
  - Change banner order
- Order management:
  - View orders
  - Update status
- Stock management

Technical Requirements:
- Fully responsive (mobile-first)
- Smooth 60fps animations
- Fast loading
- Clean modern UI
- Optimized for conversions
- Preferred stack: React / Next.js
- Minimal, scalable codebase

Goal:
Create a luxury, card-driven clock shopping experience that feels premium, calm, and modern, where the entire focus is on beautifully designed product cards and fast buying.

**Refining the App's Focus**

I'm currently streamlining the "AEVO" clock app, aiming for an ultra-minimal, luxury aesthetic. The core of this updated design will be a grid layout featuring full product cards, removing extraneous elements like storytelling and "About" sections. My goal is a modern, card-driven experience.


**Developing the Product Grid**

I'm now diving into the product grid's implementation, focusing on the visual and functional aspects. I've defined a soft pastel color palette with subtle animations. The product cards will have soft corners, glass-like shadows, and responsive hover effects. The application will leverage toggles/tabs to filter the grid by "All," "Latest," "Best Seller," and "Offers" for a user-friendly browsing experience.


**Implementing the Storefront**

I'm now fully immersed in the coding. My focus is on restructuring `Home.tsx` to seamlessly blend the hero section with the product grid as the primary storefront layout. I'm enhancing `ProductCard` with hover effects and, crucially, a "Buy Now" button. I'm also planning the new admin interfaces for product and banner management with a new structure to streamline the design. My current priority is to decide on the best "quick product detail" layout for the "Buy Now" button: a `ProductModal` or simplified `ProductDetail`.


**Revising UI Structure**

I'm now revising the app's structure to match the single-page shop vision. I've updated `Home.tsx` to integrate the hero section with the product grid and filter tabs. I'm focusing on aesthetic updates to `ProductCard.tsx` and am now debating between a `CartModal.tsx` or a `QuickView.tsx` for quick buying. I'll expand the admin pages. I'll avoid AI features per the new requests.

payload.text: change the doller into indian rupees also enhance and redesign the keyfeatures section in product page

**Prioritizing Currency and Design**

I'm currently focusing on two key changes for AEVO: first, I'm prioritizing the currency switch to INR across the entire e-commerce platform. Then, I will address the enhancement and redesign of the "Key Features" section on the product page. Keeping in mind the need for maintenance, I plan to integrate the new design into the platform with minimal disruption.


**Refining Price Display Logic**

I've been drilling down on price display across AEVO. I'm checking through all the components, specifically: `constants.tsx`, `ProductCard.tsx`, `ProductDetail.tsx`, `Wishlist.tsx`, `Admin/Dashboard.tsx`, `Admin/Products.tsx`, and `store.tsx`. It's my goal to make sure currency formatting is consistent and the underlying price data handling is clean. This all requires me to address the luxury aesthetics, responsiveness, and clean code.


**Implementing Currency Formatting**

I'm now fully focused on implementing the Indian Rupee (₹) across the platform. I've decided to use `toLocaleString('en-IN')` for currency formatting to best fit our brand and target audience. I'm also starting the redesign of the "Key Features" section. Specifically, the simple grid is out, in favor of a "The Art of Precision" section with feature cards and evocative descriptions. I'm also changing the constants to INR, and updating the existing code components.

I will update the application to transition all currency references from USD ($) to Indian Rupees (₹) and perform a high-end redesign of the "Key Features" section on the Product Detail page.

### Specification of Updates:

1.  **Currency Global Transition**:
    *   Updated `constants.tsx` to reflect luxury price points in INR (e.g., ₹3,50,000 for flagship pieces).
    *   Swapped all `$` symbols with `₹` across `ProductCard`, `ProductDetail`, `AdminDashboard`, and `AdminProducts`.
    *   Implemented `en-IN` locale formatting for all prices to ensure the correct Indian numbering system (e.g., ₹1,00,000 instead of ₹100,000).

2.  **"The Anatomy of Excellence" (Redesigned Key Features)**:
    *   **Visual Shift**: Moved from a standard grid to a sophisticated, staggered "Exhibition" layout.
    *   **Artisanal Details**: Added decorative serif numbering (01, 02, etc.) for each feature to evoke a "limited edition" catalog feel.
    *   **High-Contrast Design**: Each feature block now utilizes a refined combination of ivory backgrounds, gold iconography, and charcoal typography.
    *   **Micro-interactions**: Implemented a "Reveal & Rise" hover effect where the gold icons glow and the background shifts slightly, creating a tactile digital experience.
    *   **Content Enrichment**: Descriptions have been rewritten with more evocative, luxury-focused copy.

3.  **UI Refinements**:
    *   The "Acquire Piece" section now sits within an even more prominent "Investment" card to emphasize the value proposition of the timepieces.

### Next Steps for Implementation:
1.  **Supabase Setup:** You must create a project at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com).
2.  **SQL Tables:** Run the following SQL in your Supabase SQL Editor:
    ```sql
    CREATE TABLE products (
      id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
      name TEXT NOT NULL,
      description TEXT,
      price NUMERIC NOT NULL,
      original_price NUMERIC,
      category TEXT CHECK (category IN ('Men', 'Women', 'Wall Clocks', 'Smart Clocks', 'Luxury Series')),
      tag TEXT DEFAULT 'None',
      images TEXT[] DEFAULT '{}',
      specs JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
      stock INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
      rating NUMERIC DEFAULT 5,
      reviews_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
    );

    CREATE TABLE banners (
      id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
      title TEXT NOT NULL,
      subtitle TEXT,
      image_url TEXT NOT NULL,
      tag_label TEXT DEFAULT 'Limited',
      display_order INTEGER DEFAULT 0
    );

    CREATE TABLE orders (
      id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
      user_name TEXT,
      user_email TEXT,
      total_amount NUMERIC,
      status TEXT DEFAULT 'Pending',
      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
    );
    ```
3.  **Environment Variables:** Ensure `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` are provided in your hosting environment.

This architecture ensures that every aspect of the site is controllable via the **Atelier Command Center**, while the public storefront remains lightning-fast and brand-consistent.

To implement a secure entrance to your **AEVO Atelier Portal**, I will integrate Supabase Authentication and a dedicated admin login interface. 

### Database Preparation (SQL)
Before the login screen can function, you must execute the following SQL in your Supabase SQL Editor. This sets up a `profiles` table to track who has administrative privileges:

```sql
-- 1. Create a table for user profiles with admin status
CREATE TABLE public.profiles (
  id UUID REFERENCES auth.users ON DELETE CASCADE PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT,
  is_admin BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT timezone('utc'::text, now()) NOT NULL
);

-- 2. Enable Row Level Security
ALTER TABLE public.profiles ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- 3. Policy: Users can view their own profile
CREATE POLICY "Users can view own profile" ON public.profiles
  FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = id);

-- 4. Function to automatically create a profile entry on signup
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO public.profiles (id, email, is_admin)
  VALUES (new.id, new.email, FALSE); -- Note: Set is_admin to TRUE manually for your admin account in the table editor
  RETURN new;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;

-- 5. Trigger the function on signup
CREATE TRIGGER on_auth_user_created
  AFTER INSERT ON auth.users
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE PROCEDURE public.handle_new_user();
```
